chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Jamīl ibn Darrāj from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, regarding false testimony, who said:

If the thing remains present in its very form, it is returned to its owner; and if it is no longer present, he is liable according to the amount of what he caused to be destroyed from the man's property.

key_terms.أَتْلَفَ: caused to be destroyed or lost
key_terms.الشَّيْءُ: the property or item in dispute
key_terms.شَهَادَةِ الزُّورِ: false testimony or perjured witness testimony
key_terms.قَائِمًا بِعَيْنِهِ: still existing in its original form

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on compensation for property lost through false testimony in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the consequences of false testimony when it leads to the loss of another person's property. If the property itself still exists, it must be returned to its owner; if it has been lost or destroyed, liability is established for its value.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3331 - Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu Abdullah (as), regarding false testimony.

Imam (as) said: "If the thing is present in its original form, it is returned to its owner. But if it is no longer present, then the false witness is liable for the value of what he caused to be lost from the man's property."
